business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stock Photography Marketplace and Generative Visual Assets

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (Unitary National Jurisdiction; SIFA-administered International Company regime)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: English common law heritage with local legislation and customary land law overlay; no Islamic Sharia application
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa–New Zealand Double Taxation Relief Agreement (in force)
Samoa–China Agreement on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (in force)
Tax Information Exchange Agreement with Australia (in force)
PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus), in force since 2020

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 (Samoa), as amended — customer due diligence and beneficial ownership obligations; International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, and Samoa International Finance Authority Act 2005 — SIFA-administered International Company registry and licensed registered-agent regime; Companies Act 2001 (Samoa) for domestic-law interplay; SIFA AML/CFT Guidelines for International Companies and Registered Agents. The regime is FATF/APG-aligned, requiring identification and verification of every ultimate beneficial owner at the 25% ownership threshold.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each intended director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the document holder's country of residence certifying against the original passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise Consular Legalization at the competent Samoan consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within the preceding 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or banking institution; notarized by a qualified notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder or corporate director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction company registry or licensed registered agent of the corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / source-of-funds letter for the beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Depository bank of record in the owner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and anticipated counterparties against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List (industry standard applied by Samoan banks), EU/UK consolidated sanctions, and Samoa domestic designations; enhanced due diligence is statutorily required for PEPs, family members, and close associates under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018; screening is conducted at onboarding and repeated on an ongoing, event-driven basis by the licensed registered agent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SIFA Registry (Samoa International Finance Authority International Companies Online Filing and Name Reservation System); domestic name cross-check performed through the MCIL Companies Office (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory names must be expressed in Latin-script characters of the English alphabet under the International Companies Act 1987; Samoan words are registerable when transliterated in Latin script; Chinese or other non-Latin scripts may not constitute the registered name, and any foreign-script trading name must be accompanied by a romanized English transliteration disclosed to SIFA.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any name identical or confusingly similar to an existing Samoan or International Company
Any name implying sponsorship by the Samoan Government or a foreign state
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 registry business days of a rejection, the licensed registered agent may file a written review request with the Registrar of International Companies asserting distinctiveness and attaching any ministerial consents; if the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may re-apply under a modified name or seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa within 21 days; sensitive tokens may be cleared by prior written consent of SIFA or the responsible Minister.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible: an International Company is not required to maintain physical staff, premises, or assets in Samoa, but must at all times maintain a statutory registered office at the address of a SIFA-licensed registered agent; management and control must remain outside Samoa to preserve the tax-exempt status, and the registered agent performs statutory filing and AML/CFT custody functions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this sector: approximately 2–5% annualized probability of an unannounced SIFA inspection for a low-risk stock-media platform; the probability rises materially upon adverse intelligence, PEP exposure, sanctions hits, or negative regulatory information.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and name clearance fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) via licensed registered agent

SIFA annual government license fee (year 1, payable at incorporation)
Registered agent and registered office service (first year, including UBO register custody)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding due diligence file, PEP and sanctions screening, and UBO verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Samoan registered agent / compliance officer

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and consular legalization of beneficial owner and director documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2014 (Samoa), Part II (Incorporation, ss. 5-12), Part IV (Registered Office and Agent, ss. 22-26), and Part V (Directors and Secretary, ss. 30-38)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: International Companies Registry, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued pursuant to Form IC-1 application and Filed Copy of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; share capital may be expressed in any currency, issued nil-paid or partly paid, and no escrow account or capital deposit is required for a Samoa International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT, upon recommendation of the Subscriber under the International Companies Act 2014: (1) the subscription for the initial ordinary shares be accepted; the shares be recorded in the register of members and issued with consideration in accordance with the Subscription Agreement; (2) the registered office of the Company in Samoa at the address of the licensed registered agent be adopted, and the agent be authorised to give all statutory notices to the Registry; (3) the individuals named in the consent forms be appointed as director and secretary, each to act singly, subject to the Articles; and (4) the secretary or registered agent be authorised to execute all incorporation filings and certificates. This resolution may be executed on paper or electronically.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: International Companies Registry, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-NR electronically through a licensed registered agent or the SIFSA online portal. The proposed name must not be identical or nearly identical to any existing Samoa International Company or prohibited designation. Obtain a name availability certificate before preparing the constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application Form IC-NR
Copy of proposed members' identification documents
Letter from licensed registered agent confirming name search result
Draft memorandum and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for conflict or undesirability, file a fresh Form IC-NR with a distinguishing addition, or submit a written consent from the earlier name holder to permit similarity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of State Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: International Companies Registry, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-1 together with the approved memorandum and articles, registered agent consent, and director/secretary consents. Pay the prescribed state filing fee via bank transfer to the SIFSA Registry account. The subscriber signatures must be witnessed and, where required by the agent, notarised before electronic lodgment.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 with subscriber declarations
Notarised or witnessed subscriber identity documents
Approved memorandum and articles of association
Consent of the proposed registered agent
Consent of each proposed director and secretary
Government filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Registry will issue a compliance query within 14 days if documents are incomplete. Correct and resubmit the deficient items within 30 days; if the window lapses, tender a new application with a further fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: International Companies Registry, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notice of registered office and registered agent address in Samoa on Form IC-RO. The registered office must be an active physical address in Samoa provided by a licensed registered agent, and the agent must accept service of process on behalf of the international company.
required_dossiers: Form IC-RO
Registered agent acceptance letter
Physical address proof of the registered office
Power of attorney in favour of the registered agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects the address due to non-recognition of the premises, instruct the registered agent to provide a compliant business address and submit an amended Form IC-RO before the certificate is sealed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: International Companies Registry, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After verification of the application and payment, the Registrar enters the company in the International Companies Register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the official seal of SIFSA. Obtain a certified copy of the certificate and registered memorandum from the Registry.
required_dossiers: Acknowledgement of incorporation issued by the Registry
Received full payment of state fees
Certified copy of the memorandum and articles
Original Form IC-1 as filed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical error in the company name or date, return the original certificate to the Registrar within 30 days for administrative rectification without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Governance Machinery Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent in Samoa, acting under the International Companies Act 2014
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold or adopt the first board resolution covering share allotment, registered office confirmation, and officer appointments. Issue share certificates, open the register of members and register of directors, and ensure the company's common seal and electronic signing requirements are installed in accordance with the Articles.
required_dossiers: Pro forma first board resolution
Minutes of the first board meeting
Share certificates issued to subscribers
Register of members and register of directors
Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any officer consents or board act is challenged by the Registry, file remedial officer consents and a confirmatory board resolution; repeat any defective issuance of shares by reallotment under the same subscriber approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the business is an exclusively digital stock photography marketplace and generative visual asset service with no industrial manufacturing or physical processing plant; any future physical office licence would be administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) and the Apia City licensing authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no industrial operating permit or manufacturing licence is required for a non-physical digital media platform under Samoa law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based digital enterprise generating no effluent, no point-source emissions and no noise beyond incidental IT operations; no Environmental Impact Assessment is triggered under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharge or combustion emissions arise from the stock media platform. Where server-hosting equipment is located in a leased commercial office, electronic waste must be disposed of through an approved e-waste recycler under the Waste Management Act 2016, and electronic equipment must satisfy the applicable voltage and heat-dissipation electrical safety standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No heavy industrial fire clearance is required. The leased office must obtain a standard building compliance certificate covering electrical wiring safety, fire extinguisher placement, unobstructed emergency exits, and structural load capacity for IT racks; employers must maintain an occupational first-aid kit and conduct annual fire and earthquake drill logs in accordance with the Samoa National Building Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) — Ministry for Revenue; Official web portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws/ (Tax Administration System online services)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must submit the prescribed Application for Tax Identification Number (TIN) to the Samoa Revenue Authority via the Tax Administration System, including the Certificate of Incorporation under the International Companies Act 1987, a certified copy of the Memorandum and Articles of Association, a completed Foreign Ownership Declaration, an original Certified Public Accountant (CPA) or legal practitioner certification of the entity's valid existence, a local registered address, and proof of the authorized agent's identity; the application is reviewed by the TIN Unit and a 9-digit TIN is issued upon approval, with a Taxpayer Identification Card; there is no requirement for local economic substance for the mere issuance of a TIN, but the TIN must be filed for VAGST and customs purposes if the entity conducts any taxable activity in Samoa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available under Samoa domestic law; an International Company is statutorily classified as a non-resident exempt entity under the International Companies Act 1987, and may elect to be treated as an ordinary resident company for Samoa income tax purposes only if it obtains a formal tax residence certificate from the SRA and files a voluntary election on Form IT-ELEC-01, subject to the Minister for Revenue's discretion; hybrid mismatch elections are not permitted in Samoa, and any entity attempting to exploit inconsistent treatment between jurisdictions may be subject to general anti-avoidance rules under the Income Tax Act 2012, Schedule 2 (GAAR provisions).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (Samoa Tālā) annual taxable turnover threshold; businesses supplying goods or services in Samoa must register for VAGST within 14 days after the end of the month in which the threshold is reached or exceeded; overseas suppliers of digital services or electronic goods to Samoan consumers are subject to a separate offshore supplier registration regime effective from 1 January 2022, with an optional simplified registration for non-resident electronic marketplace operators.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-connected e-invoicing clearance regime is currently operative in Samoa; however, SRA requires electronic filing of VAGST returns and payment via the Tax Administration System, and businesses must issue sequential, serially numbered tax invoices (VAGST invoice) containing the supplier's name, TIN, invoice date, description, quantity, price, VAGST amount, and serial number; invoice records must be retained for a minimum of 7 years and made available on SRA request; the SRA has announced plans to pilot an electronic tax invoice registry for large taxpayers, but no binding secondary legislation has been enacted as of the knowledge cutoff.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: In accordance with the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2003 (Section 22 and VAGST Regulations), a registered person may zero-rate supplies of goods that are physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of the time of supply, provided that the supplier retains evidence of export; zero-rating for services applies only to services supplied to a non-resident recipient for use entirely outside Samoa, excluding services relating to land or goods situated in Samoa; digital stock photography and generative visual asset licensing services qualify for zero-rating where the non-resident customer acquires digital download rights and the payment is received into a Samoa-licensed bank account; the zero-rating must be claimed in the VAGST return by reference to the export vend code.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Export Declaration (Customs Form ED-1) stamped by the Samoa Customs Division
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing the physical departure of goods (for goods); for digital services, a contractual service schedule and server-upload timestamp log
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank receipt evidencing foreign currency payment from the non-resident buyer
Commercial invoice or tax invoice marked 'Zero-rated export' with reference to VAGST Act provisions
Proof of non-resident status of the purchaser (e.g., utility bill, registry extract, or passport/ID)
Certificate of Digital Delivery / download log from the stock photo platform
A signed declaration from the exporter attesting to the absence of local consumption in Samoa
Insurance certificate and packing list when applicable to physical goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SRA may conduct post-export verification audits within 5 years of the zero-rating claim; if the export documentation is found to be false, missing, or fabricated, the entire zero-rated output tax must be clawed back and assessed as 15% VAGST, plus overdue late payment penalties of 2% per month on the unpaid tax and a late filing penalty of WST 1,000 for each defective return; in addition, the VAGST Act 2003 Section 49 imposes a criminal penalty of a fine not exceeding WST 100,000 or up to 5 years imprisonment for willful evasion, and Customs Act 2014 applies to customs documentation fraud with forfeiture of goods and a fine of up to WST 200,000; further, a fraudulent zero-rating claim under common law may constitute deception, and the entity can be deregistered from VAGST indefinitely.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Apia - the monetary authority established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; the CBS administers the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Exchange Control Regulations 1977 and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 (as amended), licenses all commercial banks, and delegates defined exchange-control functions to authorized dealers under CBS-published delegated limits. The Minister of Finance retains residual exchange-control power; the Registrar of International Companies (within the Samoa International Finance Authority / Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour) administers the International Company registry.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is not freely convertible on an open-market basis; the CBS operates a managed float against a trade-weighted basket and requires all WST conversion to flow through authorized dealers. Current-account transactions (cloud hosting, SaaS subscriptions, contributor royalties, professional fees) are remittable within authorized-dealer delegated limits; amounts above the applicable threshold require a CBS exchange-control application. The capital account is restricted: a non-resident carrying on business inside Samoa requires certification under the Foreign Investment Act 2020, but a purely offshore International Company that markets digital stock-photo and generative visual licenses exclusively to non-residents maintains no domestic business footprint and therefore sits outside the domestic investment-licensing and capital-transfer perimeter. Profit distributions and shareholder-loan repayments to foreign owners require a foreign-exchange application supported by management/audited accounts and confirmation that the funds were earned offshore; approval is routinely granted where monies are held in an external USD account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident exporters, CBS practice requires repatriation of export proceeds within three months of export/settlement and surrender of eligible proceeds into WST through an authorized dealer unless a foreign-currency retention facility is approved. The Samoa International Company is non-resident and its stock-photo and AI-visual licensing income is an offshore service export; the statutory surrender and conversion obligation therefore does not attach, and USD may remain offshore or in an external USD account at an authorized dealer. Treasury policy must nevertheless prohibit crediting revenue into a domestic WST-denominated account; any accidental WST credit must be reversed via an exchange-control restoration application before offshore disbursement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account - USD External (non-resident) multi-currency operating account with client-money segregation sub-ledger
Operational Account - USD non-resident current account with SWIFT MT103 disbursement capacity
Operational Account - WST/USD domestic clearing account
Operational Account - domestic retail-oriented account; unsuitable as primary offshore IC treasury

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Conditional Medium-Low. Samoa has no EMI or digital-bank licensing regime; an unlicensed offshore EMI cannot act as the IC's primary custodian without exposing the entity to CBS 'unlicensed banking business' risk. Stripe does not list Samoa as a supported merchant country and PayPal's Samoan coverage is limited, so the operative model is merchant-of-record/aggregator settlement: Stripe, PayPal, or a licensed US/UK EMI (Stripe Treasury, Airwallex, Currencycloud, Wise Platform) collects card payments and wires net USD proceeds to the IC's external USD account at ANZ Bank or BSP Samoa via SWIFT MT103. The EMI may be used strictly as a pass-through collection and disbursement rail with zero overnight balance retention; all store-of-value, contingency reserves, and escrow balances must sit with a licensed Samoan authorized dealer or a CBS-recognized correspondent institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is the default: Samoan authorized dealers generally require at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner to attend a physical onboarding interview at the Apia branch, or a notarized identity ceremony at a Samoan consulate or registered-agent office, to satisfy the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 (as amended) and CBS beneficial-ownership directives. Remote video onboarding is accepted only case-by-case for low-risk ICs where the registered agent is a Samoa-licensed trust or corporate-services provider, the bank has an existing correspondent relationship, and directors provide notarized passports, bank references, and a legal-opinion cover from Samoan counsel; in practice the first signatory mandate must be notarized and any physical-interview waiver requires approval by the bank's Money Laundering Compliance Officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt IC with a nominee/trust structure and no visible physical substance in Samoa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum & Articles under the International Companies Act 2012; registered-agent certificate; beneficial-ownership register filed with the Registrar of International Companies; board resolutions appointing signatories; group structure chart with UBO passports and proof of tax residence; marketplace and subscription contracts evidencing active offshore licensing business; cloud-hosting and domain invoices; legal opinion from Samoa counsel confirming non-resident and tax-exempt status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume low-value micro-payouts flowing to third-party photographers, AI-content contributors, and artist/model payees through aggregators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Settlement statements from Stripe/PayPal; contributor payout ledger with ISIC 7420-aligned invoice trail; platform terms confirming the IC as merchant of record; contributor KYC and sanctions-screening logs; historical payout reconciliation; board-approved payout policy; content-provenance and watermark governance policy for AI-generated visual assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inflows from US/EU online aggregators combined with outflows to jurisdictions perceived as crypto-augmented or copyright-risk (P2P, generative-AI marketplaces).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Originator bank details and payment-purpose codes on each SWIFT credit; source-of-funds questionnaire; jurisdiction allowlist/blocklist policy; AML transaction-monitoring procedures; digital-licensing agreements and IP-rights documentation; quarterly external audit or attestation of treasury flows; rapid-response pack pre-assembled for CBS enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA/CRS classification mismatch of a tax-exempt entity with US-Person shareholders or US-source digital income.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid W-8BEN-E and CRS self-certification forms; entity-classification chart distinguishing the IC from a passive NFFE; US-nexus analysis showing no fixed place of business in the US; Samoa tax-exemption certificate from the Ministry of Revenue; annual self-certification of continued non-resident status and AEOI exchange classification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route: parent/shareholder sends a SWIFT MT103 USD credit from a correspondent bank free of sanctions exposure to the IC's external USD account at the authorized dealer, with narration 'IC share capital / capital contribution' and the CBS balance-of-payments reporting classification 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' (BPM6-aligned code as mapped on the bank's payment-purpose schedule, e.g., 5101 equivalent). The bank files the CBS capital-inflow return; prior CBS approval is not required for a normal equity injection through the company's own authorized dealer unless the applicable dealer delegated limit is exceeded, in which case a CBS application must be submitted pre-funding. No statutory minimum capitalization applies to a Samoa International Company, but the bank's onboarding committee will expect a board resolution confirming the capital quantum is for working capital, licensing acquisitions, and contributor-ledger reserves; shareholder loans require a signed facility letter and investor source-of-wealth documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail is SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) for contributor royalties, cloud/bandwidth charges, legal and audit fees, and capital repatriation; MT202/MT202COV supports interbank treasury concentration between ANZ/BSP Samoa and US or New Zealand correspondents. Commercial letters of credit are technically available at Samoan commercial banks but are not appropriate for digital-service disbursements and should be excluded from the stock-photo/generative-AI licensing flows. For local Samoa costs (registered-agent fees, registrar fees, legal retainers) the IC converts a bounded USD amount to WST through the authorized dealer at the CBS-supervised interbank rate plus standard dealer margin; every foreign-currency disbursement must be supported by an underlying invoice and an exchange-control payment-purpose code to remain audit-ready for CBS inspection.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST spot conversion through an authorized dealer at CBS-supervised rates (non-discretionary).
USD/WST outright forward with the authorized dealer for hedging known WST expenditure, within the dealer's CBS delegated limit and only with documented underlying commercial exposure.
Cross-currency swap (USD to WST or EUR to WST) with a licensed dealer, subject to prior CBS exchange-control approval and proof of cash-flow matching.
Natural-hedging and currency-netting policy: maintain USD as the functional treasury currency, bill and pay in USD, and hold only minimal WST balances to eliminate derivative dependence.
NDF on WST is not available in the domestic Samoan market and offshore NDF execution would require a specific CBS exemption; not recommended for this IC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 1 January of each calendar year; for a company incorporated after 1 January, the prorated fee for the remainder of the licence year is payable at incorporation and subsequent annual renewals fall due on the following 1 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee penalty of 10% per month or part thereof; continued non-payment for 90 days permits the Registrar to give 30 days' strike-off notice and to remove the International Company from the register without winding up; all assets and powers of a struck-off company vest in the Government of Samoa.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form AR-IC) with Declaration of Registered Office and Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the anniversary date of incorporation; the annual return must contain the current directors, shareholders, registered office, and registered agent as at the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of WS$50 per month or part of a month; where the annual return remains outstanding for six months, the Registrar may initiate administrative strike-off proceedings and may also direct the registered agent to cease acting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) AML/CFT Supervision Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of each year; any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding percentages must be reported to the registered agent within 14 days after the underlying change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalty of up to WS$200 per non-compliance occurrence; repeated non-compliance may result in revocation of the registered agent's licence, administrative enforcement against the company, and investigative action by SIFA.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to Samoa International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987; an independent audit becomes mandatorily required only when (i) shareholders holding not less than 10% of voting rights request an audit, or (ii) the Samoa International Finance Authority issues a formal direction requiring audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act 1987 accounting records standard; where financial statements are prepared for audit, they must follow International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or a local GAAP acceptable to the auditors; the company is exempt from public filing of financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must obtain an annual written confirmation from the International Company identifying each beneficial owner's full legal name, nationality, residential address, and precise shareholding percentage; this confirmation must be completed on or before 31 January each year. The registered agent must transmit any beneficial-ownership update to SIFA within 14 days of receipt and must retain the confirmation transcript and underlying ownership records for a minimum of seven years.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,500 per annum (inclusive of registered office, registered agent, and corporate secretarial services).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 4,500 per voluntary audit engagement (no compulsory statutory audit applies to this International Company).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Samoa International Companies are wholly exempt from Samoan corporate income tax on worldwide profits under section 150 of the International Companies Act 1987. There is no capital gains tax, no stamp duty on IC share transfers, and no Samoan GST/VAT on offshore licensing revenue. The only recurring mandatory state levy is the annual International Companies Registry licence fee.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return form exists for an International Company. Samoa Inland Revenue does not require an IC to register for income tax or file a tax return. The only periodic compliance instrument is the Annual Return of an International Company (Registry Form 4), submitted through the Samoa International Companies Registry online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annually for registry compliance; nil income tax filing frequency.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual registry return is due within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation. The annual government licence fee is payable by 1 April of each calendar year. No income tax deadline is triggered for an IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International Company name, certificate number, and registered office address in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the licensed registered agent's Samoan office address; do not declare tax residency in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of directors and shareholders, including nominee positions and beneficial ownership details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners must be identified for Anti-Money Laundering purposes; no Samoan tax identification number is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of regulated versus non-regulated business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a stock photography and generative visual assets business, declare non-regulated offshore business; do not claim local operating licence status unless Samoa consumer-facing activity exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No late income tax filing penalty arises because no income tax return is required. Late annual registry return and fee filings attract a monthly surcharge of SAT 500 per month under the International Companies Act 1987, with continued default leading to strike-off, restoration penalties, and potential director disqualification.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No Samoan tax treaty relief application is necessary for dividends paid by an International Company because Samoan domestic law imposes zero withholding tax on such distributions. An IC is not a Samoan tax resident and cannot obtain a Samoan Tax Residency Certificate; therefore, no TRC should be sought from Samoa Inland Revenue. If a shareholder in a treaty jurisdiction attempts to claim foreign tax credit relief, the relevant treaty application is made in the shareholder's country of residence, not in Samoa.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on royalties and interest paid by an International Company is 0%. Under the Samoa-Australia and Samoa-New Zealand double taxation agreements, treaty rates may be available only to a resident of the other contracting state; a Samoan International Company, being exempt and non-resident for tax purposes, cannot invoke or pass on treaty relief. Cross-border payments should be structured through the beneficial owner's resident jurisdiction with legal ownership documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Local File or Master File threshold is triggered for a Samoa International Company because it is outside the Samoan income tax net. For a hypothetical Samoa-resident taxpayer under the Income Tax Act 2015, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is required for controlled transactions exceeding SAT 1,000,000 per annum. For the IC structure, properly documented intercompany contracts for stock photo licensing fees are prudent but not a tax-filing obligation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019 applies to International Companies carrying on relevant activities. For a stock photography and generative AI visual assets business, the material activity will be classified as an IP business if the IC holds copyrights, licensing income, or royalty-generating digital assets. That classification requires demonstrable economic substance in Samoa: local board meetings with real decision-making, a physical registered office or premises, qualified in-country employees commensurate with the activity, and adequate annual operating expenditure. An IC that operates as a passive asset-holding vehicle without engaging in active trade is outside the relevant activity net but must still file the annual Economic Substance notification with the Registrar.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Foreign Anti-Abuse Recharacterisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoa International Company to hold all stock photo and AI visual asset licensing revenue while the real commercial management, content library, and decision-making remain entirely outside Samoa and no economic substance is maintained.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign revenue authorities may recharacterise the IC's profits as taxable in the place of effective management, apply controlled foreign corporation rules, and impose penalties of up to 100% of the understated tax with interest. In Samoa, knowingly making a false declaration to the Registrar is an offence under the International Companies Act 1987 attracting fines up to SAT 100,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign substance declarations without verifying real activity are personally liable for civil restitution of diverted profits, may be subject to foreign tax collection orders, travel bans, and imprisonment for false declaration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC as a pure mailbox during global tax audits while booking stock photo platform revenues through Samoa and failing to maintain the required local office, employees, board minutes, and decision-making records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019, failure to satisfy the economic substance test attracts a fixed penalty of SAT 50,000 plus a daily surcharge of SAT 1,000. Persistent non-compliance leads to mandatory strike-off of the IC and disclosure to foreign competent authorities under the exchange of information framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for civil penalties and restoration costs; court-imposed travel bans can be issued during the regulatory investigation, and wilful non-compliance is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Stripe and PayPal settlement proceeds into the IC bank account without conducting customer due diligence on stock photo contributors, verifying source of funds, and maintaining beneficial ownership registers as required under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 exposes the IC to financial penalties up to SAT 500,000 and account freezes by the Samoan Financial Intelligence Unit; the registered agent and licensed bank also face administrative sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for failing to file suspicious transaction reports; imprisonment up to 10 years, mandatory restitution of laundered proceeds, and travel restrictions are available sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Director Misrepresentation and False Registry Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A nominee director signing the Annual Return, economic substance declaration, and tax-exemption documents without actual oversight of the AI stock photography business or knowledge of the beneficial owner's commercial operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: False filing under the International Companies Act 1987 is a criminal offence carrying fines of up to SAT 20,000 per false instrument, disqualification from acting as a director for up to 10 years, and mandatory compensation to parties harmed by the misrepresentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors cannot hide behind limited liability; courts routinely pierce the corporate veil, impose personal civil restitution, issue travel bans, and order imprisonment for wilful false certification enabling offshore tax abuse.
